{{Top}}
{{Otheruses|Bounty hunter}}
[[File:EotE_GMK_front_character_art.png|thumb|right|250px|A pair of bounty hunters]]
{{Quote|One who takes people for money?''"<br />"''A bounty hunter.|The Murakami orchid and Hestizo Trace|<ref name="Red Harvest (novel)">[[Red Harvest (novel)|''Red Harvest'']]</ref>}}
'''Bounty hunters''' were individuals that primarily worked to capture or kill fugitives and others with a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on their head. As [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], they were also known to do other jobs for the right price, including the protection of clients. The most infamous bounty hunters were clever, resourceful, and relentless, making them very dangerous to those with wealthy enemies.

As a profession, bounty hunting was organized and regulated by various guilds, such as the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. Bounty hunters occasionally formed partnerships, though partnering with a fellow bounty hunter could be very dangerous business, as they typically valued their personal gain&mdash;and survival&mdash;above that of their companions. Despite their political neutrality and independence, many bounty hunters were effective "[[Jedi hunter/Legends|Jedi killers]]," which made their services desirable to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. There were often rivalries between bounty hunters and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] serving the same clients, notably between [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].

==Description==
Bounty hunters engaged in the practice of hunting down other [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings who were the target of a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] contract. Hunters had varied reasons for taking on a bounty. Some did it to bring fugitives and criminals to justice, others did it for more personal reasons such as tracking down their enemies or those that had wronged their masters. The best bounty hunters were those who were able to remain emotionally detached from the quarry they hunted.<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

Bounty hunters either captured or killed their target depending on the conditions of the bounty. Some stipulated a live capture as the fugitive was intended to face a trial, or because the bounty issuer wanted to kill the target themselves. Some bounty hunters refused to kill as a personal choice. Regardless of the method used, bounty hunters still had to prove they had completed the contract, usually by producing the quarry.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

While bounty hunters respected their profession, they did not respect all of their fellow hunters. They were particularly disdainful towards hunters who, in their opinion, made the profession look bad. Bounty hunters who took the lives of innocents during their hunts, or who broke a contract, often found themselves targeted by a bounty themselves. A successful career as a bounty hunter was also potentially dangerous; high-profile bounty hunters who engaged in high-paying contracts would often find themselves targeted by other hunters who attempted to sabotage their hunts.<ref name="RPG-Core" />

==Organization==
{{Quote|Both infamous and anonymous at the same time, Bounty Hunters are far more than mercenaries for hire - they're heirs to a professional legacy - an ancient brotherhood with a glorious history.|Unknown|<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
===The Guilds===
[[File:Bounty_Hunters_Guild.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Cradossk/Legends|Cradossk]] and [[Boushh/Legends|Boushh]], members of the Bounty Hunters' Guild.]]
There were a number of guilds associated with bounty hunters, the largest and best-known being the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. However, it was often plagued with infighting and a general lack of cooperation between its members, climaxing with its virtual self-destruction during the [[Bounty Hunter Wars]]. There were other organizations, such as the [[House Benelex]], [[Qulok's Fist]], the [[GenoHaradan]], and the [[Granse Confederacy]], that served a similar purpose.

Most [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]] were presented to a guild, unless the presenter was able to contact the hunters directly. Posted bounties would then be sent to hunters affiliated with the guild and the hunt would be on. With the exception of powerful beings like [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]], [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], or intermediaries like [[Kud'ar Mub'at]], most beings contracted hunters in this manner.

During the [[Jedi Civil War]] it was possible to merely walk into a bounty office and browse current bounties, as [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] did during his stay on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]].

===Permits===
During the Imperial Era, the Empire issued [[Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificate/Legends|Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificates]] to bounty hunters. In some cases, bounty hunters were required to lodge a [[B23-1-14 permit]] in order to collect the maximum possible bounty.

Depending on the jurisdiction, a person without a permit could earn a bounty, as was the norm in [[Lamaredd/Legends|Lamaredd]].<ref name="R">{{GamerCite|7|Reckonings}}</ref>

==Stance==
[[File:BobaFett-TotC.png|thumb|right|250px|Boba Fett accepted bounties from anyone who could pay his fee.]]
{{Quote|What's the best way to find another bounty hunter?''"<br />"''Think like him?''"<br />"''No. You hire him.|[[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] and [[Mirta Gev]]|<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>}}
Bounty hunters were almost always mistrusted and feared by locals around [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. This was because their line of work was often very dangerous, and frightening. Many famous hunters earned reputations as fearsome as the most horrific [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] and criminals. Hunters such as [[Calo Nord]], [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], and [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] became household names, though none neared the unparalleled infamy of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. Bounty hunters were not universally reviled, however. Those who followed government regulations and targeted dangerous criminals were often seen as on the side of law enforcement. On [[Haruun Kal/Legends|Haruun Kal]], many [[Balawai]] children revered bounty hunters as larger than life figures.

Generally, bounty hunters remained neutral during times of galactic conflict. They were known to favor one side or another, although never officially joining any one group. For example, the aforementioned Calo Nord worked with the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] during the [[Jedi Civil War]]; [[Hunter (individual)|the Grand Champion of the Great Hunt]] worked the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]; Jango Fett worked with the Separatists prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]; and Cad Bane worked with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] during the Clone Wars. Boba Fett often worked for the Empire and even had a professional relationship of mutual respect with Darth Vader. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] rarely dealt with bounty hunters, lacking the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and finding the hunters' methods contradictory to their ways of battle.

Most often, however, bounty hunters were hired by individuals&mdash;particularly criminals and crime lords. The [[Exchange]], [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]], and Jabba the Hutt were particularly fond of using them, both for their effectiveness and their availability. 

====The Republic and Bounty Hunters====
[[File:BountyHunterGroup-TCW.png|thumb|left|300px|A group of bounty hunters in operation during the Clone Wars]]
In the period before the [[Great Galactic War]], only a handful of bounty hunters attempted to ply their trade under Republic jurisdiction. Stringent laws that varied from world to world, mandatory restitution for collateral damage, and strict limitations on the use of force combined to make most Republic-sanctioned bounties commercially unviable. As a result, only the largest contracts—those backed by substantial credits and political clout—were worth the legal and financial risk. Those who did accept Republic contracts were often derided by their peers as little more than glorified bail bondsmen.<ref name=":0">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

With the outbreak of the Great War, the Republic’s relationship with independent bounty hunters grew increasingly strained. [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] factions pressed for an outright ban on bounty hunter guilds, decrying them as destabilizing mercenaries. The Ministry of Justice imposed steep taxes on every credit collected and continued to enforce low payout rates for official bounties. Faced with high operational risks and diminishing returns, most hunters chose to avoid Republic commissions altogether. By war’s end, the majority of mercenaries had come to prefer avoiding work with the Republic entirely.<ref name=":0" />

====Work with the Empire====
{{Quote|Bounty hunters? We don't need their scum.|Firmus Piett's reaction to Darth Vader hiring bounty hunters|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
[[File:BountyHunters.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Bounty hunters hired by Darth Vader to hunt down the ''Millennium Falcon''.]]
Bounty hunters were occasionally hired to conduct duties or provide information to the Empire. One [[Unidentified bounty hunter (Imperial tip)|particular]] individual provided a tip which led to a [[Ambush at Mos Eisley|raid]] to find [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] pilot [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="RS I guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>

Following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], bounty hunters Boba Fett, [[IG-88B]], [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]], [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], and [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] were hired by Darth Vader to find the starship [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], that had escaped the battle and contained Rebel leader [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Fett, after catching IG-88B trailing him and destroying him, managed to calculate the ''Falcon''{{'s}} destination as [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] and alerted the Empire, who arrived right before the ''Falcon'' did.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Upon capturing the Organa and freezing the ship's captain, Han Solo, in carbonite, the Empire gave Solo to Fett as payment. Fett, in turn, gave him to Jabba the Hutt, due to Solo having had a massive bounty put on his head by Jabba.<ref name="ESB" />

==Behind the scenes==
The "Bounty Hunter" was one of the original twenty-four character templates used by the ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'', first published in the [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|first edition rulebook]].<ref name="RPG">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref> Bounty hunter was one the five prestige classes detailed in the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook|Core Rulebook]] for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="RPG-Core" />
